verdict: Observed candidate callback costs are higher than original in every continuous condition, and no Rust benefit over matched JS is established. Prepared rendering never activates for this feature-preserving workload. Original A/A block gates fail in all continuous conditions; do not report stable performance percentages, FPS gains, or an exact causal allocation of the regression. This supports a bounded negative adoption verdict for this candidate and app path, not a rejection of Rust ownership generally.

normalization.scope: Metadata-only public copy: digits in InternalBattery-N (id=...) become <redacted>; the battery index, AC source, charge, power settings and all measured quantities are unchanged.
normalization.inputHashScope: Every inputHashes digest is SHA-256 of original raw file bytes before metadata normalization; no digest describes a normalized replacement.
